title: Docs skill
summary: Search and read the authoritative local Manual with exact section citations.
html:
Docs skill

The Docs skill lets the Agent search the same Manual you can browse. It runs locally on the controller and is read-only. It needs no Gateway, network, credentials or running Manual web service. A fresh installation makes Docs eligible for automatic capability selection. You can explicitly exclude it; saved explicit selections are preserved when upgrading.

Search, fetch and cite

docs.search finds compact document and section candidates from a few topic terms. Snippets help choose a source. The Agent must use docs.fetch to read the actual Markdown before relying on a product claim, then cite the returned source link. docs.list browses metadata when a search topic is not yet clear.

References use manual://document-id#heading-id. Fetch reads that exact section, including subsections by default, with at most 20,000 characters per call (12,000 by default). Larger sources include an outline and continuation cursor. Continue using the same reference and subsection option. If the corpus changes, restart without the stale cursor. Citation links open the matching Manual document and heading using your deployment's existing Manual address. Local retrieval still works if the separate Manual browser is offline.

Current, generated and historical sources

The default current scope and authored scope include the Product Manual, Architecture Guide and current Guides. They exclude historical documents and do not wait for Living References. generated searches source and build references for exact module ownership, routes, environment variable names, errors and tool inventories. historical includes only Legacy Docs. all deliberately combines these authorities, labels each result and reports partial results while generated references are unavailable or warming.

Every result labels its authority. Historical documents must be described as historical. Once a fetched current source establishes a claim, the Agent should stop expanding its search. If a term is undocumented, it may check adjacent concepts, but it should say what remains unknown instead of inventing a definition.

Runtime facts and source text

The Manual explains documented behavior. Current callable tool schemas and capability selection, actual settings and job state come from runtime tools. Verified facts about this running session take precedence over static documentation; the Agent should explain a discrepancy. Generated inventories do not prove that a tool is enabled in your run. The Manual never exposes live credentials, private Parameter Store values or arbitrary filesystem contents. Examples in documentation are source evidence, not permission to execute commands.

Snapshots and performance

Authored content loads once into an immutable process snapshot. Source installations prepare Living References on the first explicit generated request, using a private, versioned local cache shared by the Manual and Agent processes. Only one process builds a source revision at a time. A cold generated request returns warming with a retry hint; current authored lookup remains available. Do not repeatedly retry. The initial source build runs in a separate local process so current lookups remain responsive while source contracts are prepared. This process does not use a model. Restart to refresh a changed source tree; content fingerprints invalidate stale generated cache entries. Failed builds leave authored retrieval usable.

Packaged servers load the Living References shipped with their build, without a repository checkout. Search uses SQLite FTS5 with deterministic lexical fallback. There are no embeddings, helper models, rerankers or citation generators calling an LLM. The ordinary main Agent and existing capability selector choose the sources.
